author: NorthEast News Desk
body: London equities recovered on Friday as crude oil retreated, but the rebound was not enough to prevent a difficult week for major British indexes. The FTSE 100 and the domestically focused FTSE 250 each closed about 0.4% higher for the session.

Banks helped lead the recovery, with HSBC up 1.5% and Barclays gaining 1.9% in the reported session. Construction and materials shares rose about 1.8%. Softer oil prices provided some relief after energy costs had added to concern about inflation and the path of interest rates.

Despite Friday’s gain, the FTSE 100 recorded its largest weekly decline since late July, while the FTSE 250 posted its steepest weekly loss in more than four months. Traders were pricing roughly 44 basis points of Bank of England rate increases by year-end at the time of the report. Those figures describe Friday’s close and contemporaneous expectations, not live prices. The split between a positive final session and a negative week shows how energy markets and rate assumptions continued to drive short-term sentiment across British shares.
dek: The FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 each added 0.4% Friday, yet both finished a volatile week with substantial declines.
headline: London shares rebound Friday but post steep weekly losses
